# Build your own interactive webmap

Learn how to create a webmap from the ground up using **OpenLayers**, an open-source JavaScript library for web mapping.

You will start with a basic map and gradually develop it by adding geospatial data, adjusting the map view, styling layers and building interface elements. By the end, you will have a working webmap that you can publish online.

**You do not need to be an experienced programmer to complete the exercises.** However, you should be comfortable working with files and folders, and be prepared to edit some HTML, CSS and JavaScript code.


[Start the tutorial →](01-setup.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}

## What you will learn

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.learning-card}

### Add geospatial data

Load a WMS layer from a remote geospatial service and display local GeoJSON datasets.

:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.learning-card}

### Configure the map

Adjust the map view, style vector layers, switch basemaps and build a legend.

:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.learning-card}

### Build and publish

Add a title and information panel, then publish the finished application using GitHub Pages.

:::
:::

## The tutorial

Work through the chapters in order. Each chapter introduces a new element of the webmap and builds on the code from the previous exercise.

| Chapter | Topic |
|:--|:--|
| 01 | Setup and project structure |
| 02 | Add a WMS layer |
| 03 | Configure the map view |
| 04 | Add GeoJSON layers |
| 05 | Style vector layers |
| 06 | Add a basemap switcher |
| 07 | Create a legend |
| 08 | Add a map title |
| 09 | Create an information panel |
| 10 | Publish the webmap |

## Before you begin

You will need a code editor, Node.js and a basic understanding of working with files and folders. You will edit HTML, CSS and JavaScript as you progress through the exercises.

Start with [Chapter 1: Setup](01-setup.qmd) to prepare your working environment.

## About this resource

This tutorial is a practical learning resource used in Master's level Geography teaching at the University of Turku. It is maintained by UTU Geospatial Labs.
